name: Grand Valley

climate: Seasons this warm ripen Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, Cabernet Franc, Tempranillo and Dolcetto fully without cooking off their freshness.
Merlot and Cabernet Sauvignon sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.
Riesling is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.
Chardonnay is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.
Rain picks up at harvest. Growers race to pick before rot sets in, and vintages vary more.

soil.rock: Gravel drains fast and is poor, so roots go deep for water and food. It holds little water. Shale and mudstone are fine-grained rocks that hold heat well and are moderately fertile.
soil.top: The topsoil holds water well and drains at a steady pace, so vines rarely go thirsty or sit in wet ground. Its high pH can starve vines of iron and yellow the leaves, so growers plant lime-tolerant rootstocks.

land: Mostly flat. Easy and cheap to farm by machine, but on still nights cold air settles on flat ground, so spring frost is a bigger risk.

winkler: Good for generous crops of standard to good wine.
